title: Wash home only: one intensity token --gamecult-wash multiplies every ground radial's alpha; 1 on / and 0.5 elsewhere; the ritual ground follows the same token
first: Map: docs/masthead-campaign.md, section 'One column' (map revision 4), facts C6 and the paragraph 'Wash'. Ruling: operator-chromeless-column ('that background wash gets too bright on pages that aren't the homepage'). Line numbers from 535d170; re-read by selector.

Surfaces: body (10-29) paints three radials over the navy gradient: orange rgba(255,138,42,.18), violet rgba(109,96,255,.16), sky rgba(89,183,255,.14). The three ritual essays' body block (103-124) paints its own ground: yellow rgba(255,178,30,.15), cobalt rgba(49,88,255,.22), violet rgba(91,54,184,.19) over its own gradient. tour/Pitch cover the body with the VN; /Thing's hero paints .hero-bg in the Eve deck.css and is not the site's wash; the .page::before grid overlay (39-50) is not the wash and is untouched.

Mechanism: one token on body, --gamecult-wash: 0.5, and one home override, body[data-slug="index"] { --gamecult-wash: 1; }. Each radial's alpha becomes calc(<its literal> * var(--gamecult-wash)) in modern colour syntax, e.g. rgb(255 138 42 / calc(0.18 * var(--gamecult-wash))). The literals keep their current values so the home page is byte-for-byte the same wash and every other page is half.

The Self's heads-up (not a ruling): the operator may later paint the ground with a WebGL shader. The CSS wash stays as the fallback; the shader would read --gamecult-wash as its intensity. So: no per-page wash rule anywhere, no second token, no class toggled by script.

Sass: dart-sass emits rgb()/rgba() whose argument contains var() or calc() as plain CSS. Confirm in the built stylesheet (public/index.css after a build, or the deployed CSS) that the calc survives; if Sass rewrote it, use the rgb(... / calc()) form, which it never evaluates. Do not reach for Sass math or a mixin.
